14: The Q&A visual lets users type natural-language questions and automatically generates a matching visual without any report redesign.
27: Remove Duplicates discards repeated rows that share identical values, leaving a single record per customer.
28: Split Column divides a single column into multiple columns using a delimiter (such as a space) or fixed positions.
30: Append Queries stacks rows from tables that share the same column structure into a single combined table. Merge Queries instead joins tables side by side on a key.
31: Changing the column data type to Date ensures Power BI recognizes the values as dates so DAX time-intelligence functions and date calculations work correctly.
35: Replace Values substitutes specific text values (such as "Y"/"N") with new values (such as "Yes"/"No") throughout a column.
45: Dimension tables hold descriptive attributes used to filter, group, and slice the numeric data stored in fact tables like Sales.
50: CALCULATE combined with FILTER restricts the rows summed to only those where Sales Amount exceeds 1,000, correctly modifying the filter context. SUMX iterates rows but does not filter them with a boolean condition.
51: COUNTROWS counts the number of rows remaining in a table after filters are applied, which is the correct way to count transactions.
52: SELECTEDVALUE returns the single selected value from a column when exactly one value is in context, and returns blank (or a specified alternate result) when multiple values are selected.
54: RELATED retrieves a column value from a related table in a calculated column when an active relationship exists between the tables.
55: REMOVEFILTERS clears filters from the specified table or column while leaving filters on other tables untouched, unlike ALL which can be used more broadly.
59: DATEADD shifts a date column forward or backward by a specified interval (such as one month), making it the standard function for period-over-period comparisons.
61: CALENDARAUTO scans all date columns in the model and automatically builds a contiguous date table spanning the full range found, without requiring fixed start/end dates.
62: USERELATIONSHIP activates a specified inactive relationship for the duration of a single measure's evaluation, allowing Ship Date to be used without changing the model's default active relationship.
67: Republishing the app only after validation keeps the workspace report (used for testing) separate from what business users see, since app consumers only receive updates when the app is explicitly republished.
70: Sharing a report grants access to specific individuals, making it the appropriate option for limited, one-to-one distribution rather than broad distribution to a department.
71: Certified endorsement signals that content has completed an organization's formal governance review and is trusted as authoritative. Promoted is self-nominated and does not require formal review.
74: Updating the credentials stored for the data source in the Power BI Service is the direct fix when a scheduled refresh fails due to a changed password.
76: View As lets a report author preview the report exactly as a user assigned to a specific RLS role would see it, without needing to publish or log in as that user.
77: Scheduled refresh reloads an Import-mode semantic model with the latest source data at a configured time, such as every morning at 7:00 AM.
79: Since cloud sources refresh successfully and the gateway itself is online, the next thing to check is whether the on-premises data source is correctly mapped and has valid credentials configured within the gateway.
90: Denormalizing the Category attributes directly into the Product dimension removes an unnecessary relationship hop, simplifying the model into a cleaner star schema and improving performance.
91: USERELATIONSHIP inside a measure activates the inactive Ship Date relationship just for that calculation, without disturbing the default Order Date relationship used everywhere else.
92: CALCULATE with an explicit filter argument (Product[Category]="Bikes") overrides any existing filter on that same column while still respecting filters from unrelated columns, such as Region.
93: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts the current date filter context back exactly one year, making it the standard function for year-over-year comparisons in a visual.
94: Adding an Apply button (query reduction) batches slicer selections so a query is sent only once the user finishes choosing, instead of after every individual click.
95: A Power BI app packages curated reports and dashboards into a read-only, managed experience that consumers cannot edit.
99: COUNTROWS(VALUES(Customer[CustomerID])) counts the distinct customers remaining in context after the Sales relationship filters which customers have at least one order.
100: A Matrix visual supports drillable row/column hierarchies, letting users expand and collapse Region and Product Category levels while keeping data in a tabular layout.
101: The Folder connector combines all files with a matching structure found in a folder and automatically picks up new files on refresh, requiring no query changes.
102: Using USERELATIONSHIP inside only the one measure that needs Ship Date keeps the model's default Order Date relationship active for every other measure.
103: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR returns the equivalent date range from one year earlier, which is the standard pattern for comparing current revenue to the prior year.
107: Append Queries stacks rows from two queries with matching columns into a single combined table, which is the correct operation for combining customers from two systems.
108: A SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR measure plotted alongside current sales in a line or column chart visually shows which products increased or decreased compared to the prior year.
111: Adding an Apply button to slicers (query reduction) delays query execution until the user finishes adjusting all selections, reducing the number of queries sent to the model.
